flawed_step: Lines 0040-0044 (restating 0030-0033): from c(S∩S', T∪T') ≤ 2c(S,T) − c(u→v) < 2c(S,T) the proof concludes a contradiction with minimality of (S,T) and (S',T'). Minimality only forbids a cut of capacity < c(S,T); a single cut of capacity < 2c(S,T) is completely ordinary, so no contradiction has been derived.
counterexample: Take V = {s,a,b,t} with edges s→a (cap 1), a→t (cap 1), s→b (cap 1), b→t (cap 1). The min-cut value is 2. Two genuine minimum cuts: (S,T) = ({s,a},{b,t}) with capacity c(a→t)+c(s→b) = 1+1 = 2, and (S',T') = ({s,b},{a,t}) with capacity c(s→a)+c(b→t) = 1+1 = 2. Then S∩S' = {s}, T∪T' = {a,b,t}, and c(S∩S', T∪T') = c(s→a)+c(s→b) = 2. So the proof's decisive inequality holds: 2 = c(S∩S', T∪T') < 4 = 2c(S,T). Yet nothing is contradicted — ({s},{a,b,t}) is itself a minimum cut of capacity 2 ≥ c(S,T) = 2. Indeed for any network with positive min-cut value the strict inequality c(S∩S', T∪T') < 2c(S,T) is satisfied by legitimate minimum cuts (take S' = S: c(S,T) < 2c(S,T)). Hence the inference at lines 0040-0044 is invalid, and the proof establishes nothing about the edge u→v.
reasoning_summary: The proof's entire contradiction rests on deriving c(S∩S', T∪T') < 2c(S,T). Minimality of a cut only rules out cuts of capacity strictly below c(S,T), not below 2c(S,T); since c(S,T) > 0 in any nontrivial network, every minimum cut already satisfies this strict inequality. A four-node network with two crossing minimum cuts of capacity 2 exhibits c(S∩S', T∪T') = 2 < 4 = 2c(S,T) with no contradiction at all. The proof never uses the correct submodularity argument (c(S∩S') + c(S∪S') ≤ c(S) + c(S'), both terms ≥ min value, forcing equality and forcing the cross edges from S∩T' to T∩S' to have zero capacity); it drops the c(S∪S') term and compares against 2c(S,T) instead of c(S,T). Line 0024 is additionally self-contradictory, asserting u→v is not counted in c(S∩T', T∩S') while stating precisely the reason it is counted there.
notes: Counterexample is to an inferential step the proof relies on; the theorem statement itself is true.
